subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm balancing scope and quality here—thinking through whether this vehicle needs a full joint hierarchy or could stay mostly static, weighing simplicity against wanting features like turret rotation and barrel recoil.

Settling on a layout: a 6-wheeled hull around 10m long with a turret yaw joint, gun pitch joint, deployable stabilizer outriggers, and wheels that sink slightly into the ground plane for grounding. I'm working out the exact positions and dimensions for each joint and part, planning cylinder geometries for wheels and hubs, and setting up a helper function to place parts with bone attachments and transforms.

Now I'm defining the hull chassis as a boxy frustum shape with camo paint patches in olive and dark green, deciding against overly fancy panel textures in favor of a simpler custom paint scheme.

Extending the hull extrusion with the glacis slope, then working out wheel placement and radius so the fenders sit correctly against the hull sides, adding fender boxes as wheel guards above each wheel.

I'm computing the windscreen plane's normal and position so the glass panel sits flush with the sloped cab front, tinting it slightly blue. Then I'm moving on to the turret, planning a ring base at the joint and an extruded beveled body shape positioned behind the cab.

Now I'm laying out the railgun barrel assembly: a gun joint mounted near the turret front, twin parallel rail boxes spaced apart with a gap, and periodic spacer braces joining them along their length toward the muzzle.

I'm giving the rails a steel paint finish with dark insulators between them, adding thin cyan glow strips along the inner faces, and surrounding the rear with cylindrical capacitor coils (banded in blue glow) wrapped around the barrel axis. I'm also placing a breech block box at the rear of the gun, checking that it fits within the turret's height without clipping.

Now I'm realizing the barrel's trajectory actually collides with the cab — at its current elevation the barrel passes straight through the cab roof. I'm working through fixes: raising the gun's pitch, repositioning or shrinking the cab, offsetting it sideways, or lowering the cab's roof height to clear the barrel path, trying to find a layout where nothing overlaps.

Barrel parts get built in model space then posed via the gun bone's joint rotation. I need the turret front to have a slot where the gun barrel and breech protrude through, with the turret joint positioned so the front edge sits slightly ahead of the gun mount, letting rails emerge cleanly from the opening.

Now I'm laying out the rear equipment: ammo/power modules, radar box, generator housings, counterweight, exhaust stacks, antennas, lights, cooling fins, hatches, tool boxes, and decals. I'm also positioning the stabilizer outriggers — placing four legs between the wheel positions plus a rear spade plate, with horizontal beam boxes extending out from the hull sides.

Positioning the hydraulic leg pistons and pads...

I'm also adding a diagonal brace rod and warning stripes on the beam, then building wheel tires at radius 0.8 with hubs and bolt rings placed via small loops, plus tread lugs around each tire.

Instead of modeling individual lug boxes, I'll switch to a procedural paint approach using angle-based tread patterns computed per wheel center, which is much cheaper than dozens of extra parts. Then I'm planning the texture sheet: windscreen glass, hazard stripes, and an emblem.

I'm also sketching the color palette (olive drab, dark, tan, hazard yellow, glow cyan) and a camo paint scheme combining mottle and patches for the body.

I'm working out the extrude orientation and coordinate math for the hull so the thickness axis and outline align correctly, then placing the turret relative to the hull origin.

Now I'm shaping the hull profile itself, defining the glacis slope and deck edges with sharp bevels rather than smoothed corners, and checking that the wheel axles and ground contact points sit flush with the hull bottom. I'm also sketching where the cab sits along the deck relative to the hull's extended front section.

Working out the cab's extrusion shape and slope angle, I calculate the windscreen plane's position and offset along the slope's normal vector, then set up similar side window planes mirrored across the cab's thickness.

I'm also checking clearance for the barrel's rotation at 12° against the cab roof height, confirming the rail's rotation point sits at the trunnion joint so the bottom edge clears the deck with margin.

Now I'm working out the turret geometry—defining its hexagonal cross-section profile, thickness, and top height, then positioning the trunnion joint relative to the turret's local coordinates. I'm also sizing the turret ring as a flat cylinder at the deck interface and checking the turret's width and depth stay within the hull's footprint.

Next I'm detailing the turret roof features (hatches, sensors, angled smoke dischargers) and the trunnion housing cheeks as small cylinders flanking the gun joint. For the gun itself, I'm laying out the rail boxes along the barrel length and placing dark insulator spacer boxes at regular intervals between them.

Still placing coil rings and glow bands...

Rethinking the rear layout: adding a cooling radiator box with a grille texture on the rear face, plus two exhaust stack cylinders positioned at the rear corners to avoid overlapping the radiator.

For the sides, I'm placing stabilizer beams in the gap between the two wheels at z 1.6, and adding side skirt armor plates (fender boxes) above each wheel at z positions 3.3, 0, and -3.3.

Now I'm working out the stabiliser geometry: for each side and z position, placing the hull mount point, a connecting beam box between hull and outer point, a leg sleeve cylinder, and a thinner piston cylinder inside it.

Continuing with the piston extending down to a foot pad disc, a sleeve segment higher up, a diagonal brace rod connecting the hull to the leg, and a ball-joint sphere at the pad base for articulation.

I'm shaping a wedge-like rear spade plate that angles downward into the ground and attaches to the hull's rear, then starting to define the joint hierarchy—hull as the root, followed by turret, gun, and wheel joints on each side.

Now I'm building small helper functions to simplify part creation, like one for boxes and one for cylinders that take dimensions, color, position, bone, and orientation, plus setting up small glowing lamp boxes in red and amber tones.

I'm working out the radar dish and antenna geometry, but realizing a partial sphere cap would render backfaced and invisible, so I'm considering swapping to a lathe-based dish or just a simple box shape instead.

Now I'm sketching out the rotating scanner bar on the mast, plus planning texture assets: glass reflections, hazard stripes, a shield emblem, stenciled unit label text, grille slats, and a capacitor warning bolt icon.

I'm also thinking through how to apply hazard stripe textures to the beam geometry, deciding whether to texture the whole box or add a separate rotated plane on top with the stripe pattern to avoid stretching issues across all faces.

Now I'm figuring out placement of headlights embedded into the hull's glacis slope, computing the z-coordinate where the sloped profile intersects the lamp height, then sizing small boxes for the lamps and a darker box for the front bumper.

For fenders over the wheels, I'm sizing boxes wide enough to cover the tire width at the correct wheel height, then planning simple cylindrical axles running across the hull at wheel height to connect each wheel pair, with hub cylinders at the wheel centers.

Still tweaking the tread pattern...

For extras, I'm adding angled smoke dischargers on the turret cheeks, side stowage racks as boxes, and a commander's cupola cylinder on the roof.

I'm also sketching in a periscope glow, a cheek sensor sphere, and a small sensor box on the cab roof, aiming for around 200 parts total while verifying everything sits flush on the ground -- wheels and pads at y=0, with the spade's extruded wedge profile also bottoming out correctly.

Shaping the spade outline polygon...

I'm connecting the spade to the hull with two rod-like arm boxes extending from the hull's rear, then positioning the radiator box so its rear face stays nested within the hull's rear zone without poking through. I'm also checking that planes facing backward read correctly when viewed from behind, and starting to lay out the cab's side-window planes along the x-axis.

Working through the cab window geometry, I calculate the outline so the front edge stays safely inside the cab's sloped front panel, keeping the window centered and sized appropriately. I then place an emblem plane on the turret's side using the turret's local coordinates, and begin positioning a label plane along the hull's side for text.

The label sits above the fender line, matching the stabilizer beam positions, with correct sizing so the mirrored plane still reads properly when viewed from the opposite side. I confirm the colored texture parts keep their own hues and that glow effects apply cleanly to textured planes.

Now I'm setting up the builder code, starting with the carrier's named config and defining the hull joint with its position before continuing to more joint definitions.

Writing joint definitions...
